title: Space-valued presheaves on a small quasicategory are presentable
statement: Use the universes and presentability of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] and coherent functors and spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$ be the fixed universes, let $D$ be a $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory, and let $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ be the infinity category of $\mathcal U$-small spaces. Then $\mathcal P_{\mathcal U}(D)=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$ is presentable relative to $\mathcal U$: it admits all $\mathcal U$-small colimits and is generated under $\mathcal U$-small $\kappa$-filtered colimits by a $\mathcal U$-small family of $\kappa$-compact objects for some infinite regular cardinal $\kappa\in\mathcal U$. Compactness here means that the full mapping-space functor preserves those filtered colimits. No assumption that $D$ is the nerve of an ordinary category is made. The assertion is valid with any larger universe in place of $\mathcal U$.

source.place: Remark 5.5.3.7, printed p. 468 (any small simplicial set); applied here to a quasicategory. Online source read, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Put $B=D^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$. It is a quasicategory by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. First check local $\mathcal U$-smallness. For $F,G\in\mathcal P$, choose the $\mathcal U$-small right fibrations $E_F,E_G\to D$ supplied by [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]. Its mapping-space comparison identifies $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(F,G)$ with the Kan complex whose $n$-simplices are the maps $E_F\times\Delta^n\to E_G$ over $D$. In each degree this is a subset of the set of functions between two $\mathcal U$-small sets, and the union over $n\in\mathbb N$ is $\mathcal U$-small. Thus the full mapping space, and not just its components, has a $\mathcal U$-small model. The functor category itself fits in $\mathcal V$, since $D$ is $\mathcal U$-small and the collection of $\mathcal U$-small Kan complexes belongs to $\mathcal V$.

source.place: Section 2.2, space-valued straightening, and Section 5.1.1, presheaves; the right-fibration mapping-space and small-model statements are those of the cited transport node. Read online; not archived in literature/. The assembly and size bookkeeping are agent-written.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-spaces-small-colimits-universe], $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ has every $\mathcal U$-small simplicial colimit. Given any $\mathcal U$-small $J$ and $H:J\to\mathcal P$, uncurry it to $B\times J\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$. Let $B_0\subseteq B$ be the discrete simplicial subset of vertices. Choose a colimiting cocone at each vertex of $B$. These choices specify a map on $(B\times J)\amalg_{B_0\times J}(B_0\times J^{\triangleright})$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-parameter-cone-extension] with $P=B_0$, target $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$, and $K=J$. Every initial-vertex cocone required there is one of the chosen colimits, so an extension on $B\times J^{\triangleright}$ exists. All these data fit in $\mathcal V$; the colimits chosen are still $\mathcal U$-small spaces. The pointwise criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] says that the assembled cocone is colimiting in $\mathcal P$, and that evaluation at each vertex preserves it. This includes $J=\varnothing$. Consequently $\mathcal P$ admits all $\mathcal U$-small colimits and they are computed pointwise.

source.place: Proposition 5.1.2.2 and Corollaries 5.1.2.3-5.1.2.4, printed pp. 318-319; the prescribed pointwise assembly is the cited parameter-cone theorem. Read online; not archived in literature/. The assembly and size bookkeeping are agent-written.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound] to the singleton family with value $\mathbb N$ to choose an infinite regular $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ with $\aleph_0<\kappa$. Write $h:D\to\mathcal P$ for Yoneda. By [lem-coef-space-yoneda-density], the coherent functor $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(h_d,-)$ is naturally equivalent to evaluation at $d$. Evaluation preserves all $\mathcal U$-small colimits by step 2. When the corepresented mapping-space functor is viewed in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$, the comparison is followed by the universe inclusion $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$, which preserves these colimits by [lem-coef-spaces-small-colimits-universe]. It therefore preserves the specified $\mathcal U$-small $\kappa$-filtered colimiting cocones, in precisely the full mapping-space sense of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Each representable $h_d$ is $\kappa$-compact.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.2, printed pp. 324-325, and Proposition 5.1.6.8, printed p. 332; Definition 5.3.4.5 for compactness. The uncountable cardinal is chosen only for bounded-subdiagram bookkeeping. Read online; not archived in literature/. The assembly and size bookkeeping are agent-written.

proof.text: There is a $\mathcal U$-small set $T$ of representatives, up to simplicial isomorphism over $D$, of all pairs $(K,p)$ with $K$ a $\kappa$-small simplicial set and $p:K\to D$. Indeed, because $\kappa$ is uncountable, fewer than $\kappa$ nondegenerate simplices have fewer than $\kappa$ total simplices: each has countably many degeneracies, and regularity bounds their union. Relabel the total simplices by a subset of the fixed set $\kappa$. Degree assignments, face and degeneracy maps, and the map to the fixed small simplicial set $D$ then range over subsets and functions on fixed $\mathcal U$-small sets. Their collection belongs to $\mathcal U$; no bound by $\kappa$ on the number of representatives is asserted. For each $(K,p)\in T$, choose a colimiting cocone on $h\circ p$ using step 2, and denote its apex by $g_{K,p}$. These are choices of objects determined by universal properties. The resulting family $\mathcal G$ is $\mathcal U$-small. By steps 1-3, $\mathcal P$ is locally small, has all small $\kappa$-filtered colimits, and all vertices of $h\circ p$ are $\kappa$-compact. Thus [lem-coef-compact-small-colimits] makes every $g_{K,p}$ $\kappa$-compact. Include $K=\varnothing$, so the initial presheaf occurs in this family.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.4.15, printed p. 401, and the bounded-diagram argument in Proposition 5.3.5.12, printed p. 408. The relabeling argument is written out here. Read online; not archived in literature/. The assembly and size bookkeeping are agent-written.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal P$ be the full subcategory on all objects equivalent to members of $\mathcal G$. By local smallness from step 1 and the small family from step 4, [lem-coef-infinity-small-full-subcategory] makes $\mathcal A$ essentially $\mathcal U$-small. All its objects are $\kappa$-compact. Let $a\in\mathcal A$, choose $g\in\mathcal G$ and an equivalence $e:g\to a$ with inverse $e'$, and let $A$ be the rigidification of $\mathcal P$ used in the corepresented functors of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Precomposition with the vertices $e\in A(g,a)$ and $e'\in A(a,g)$ is strictly compatible with the associative enriched composition of $A$, so it defines enriched transformations $H_a\to H_g$ and $H_g\to H_a$, hence coherent transformations $e^*:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(a,-)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(g,-)$ and $e'^*$ in the reverse direction. At each vertex $x$ the two composites are precomposition with $e\circ e'$ and $e'\circ e$, and $e\circ e'$, $e'\circ e$ lie in the components of the identities in $A(a,a)$ and $A(g,g)$, whose sets of components are the homotopy-category morphisms; after realization a zigzag of edges gives homotopies to the identity, so each component $\operatorname{Sing}|A(a,x)|\to\operatorname{Sing}|A(g,x)|$ of $e^*$ is a homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], applied in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal P,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$, $e^*$ is an equivalence. Now let $\lambda:F\to\Delta_IL$ be a small $\kappa$-filtered colimiting cocone in $\mathcal P$, viewed as $\bar\lambda:I^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal P$. Whiskering $e^*$ with $\bar\lambda$ gives a transformation of $I^{\triangleright}$-diagrams in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ whose vertex components are components of $e^*$, so it is an equivalence by the same node. By its cocone criterion, the cocone $\operatorname{Map}(g,-)\circ\bar\lambda$, colimiting by compactness of $g$, is colimiting exactly when the maps $\operatorname{Map}(\operatorname{Map}(g,L),y)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})}(\operatorname{Map}(g,F),\Delta_Iy)$ are equivalences for every $y$. The equivalence $e^*$ and its restriction to $I$ identify these maps with the corresponding maps for $\operatorname{Map}(a,-)\circ\bar\lambda$, since functor equivalences induce equivalences on all mapping spaces by the same node. Hence $\operatorname{Map}(a,-)$ preserves $\lambda$, and $a$ is $\kappa$-compact. This verifies compactness using [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], rather than assuming the replete subcategory is literally a $\mathcal U$-small simplicial subset.

source.place: Propositions 5.4.1.7 and 5.4.1.2, printed pp. 419-423 (essential smallness from local smallness and a small family of equivalence classes), as applied in the opening of the proof of Proposition 5.3.5.12, printed p. 408. Read online; not archived in literature/. The assembly and size bookkeeping are agent-written.

proof.text: Fix $F\in\mathcal P$. By [lem-coef-space-yoneda-density], choose a $\mathcal U$-small simplicial set $E_F$, a coherent $p_F:E_F\to D$, and a colimiting cocone $h\circ p_F\to F$. For every $\kappa$-small simplicial subset $L\subseteq E_F$, choose an isomorphism over $D$ from a representative $(K,p)\in T$ to $(L,p_F|_L)$. Reindexing the chosen cocone of step 4 along this simplicial isomorphism gives a colimiting cocone on $h\circ p_F|_L$ with the same apex $q_L=g_{K,p}$. Now apply [lem-coef-colimit-subdiagram-approximation] in $\mathcal P$, using the uncountable regular $\kappa$ of step 3 and cocompleteness from step 2. Its prescribed-cocone assertion assembles these very apices into a coherent diagram $Q:N(I_\kappa(E_F))\to\mathcal P$ and a colimiting cocone $Q\to F$. The node says that $I_\kappa(E_F)$ is $\mathcal U$-small and its nerve is $\kappa$-filtered. Every vertex $q_L$ is a member of $\mathcal G$, so the entire coherent diagram factors through the full subcategory $\mathcal A$ by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. This expresses every $F$ as a $\mathcal U$-small $\kappa$-filtered colimit of objects in the same essentially small full subcategory of $\kappa$-compact objects. There is no assumption that the index has fewer than $\kappa$ simplices.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.3, printed p. 325; Proposition 4.2.3.4, Corollary 4.2.3.10, and the directed-union construction in the proof of Corollary 4.2.3.11, printed pp. 249-253; last paragraph of the proof of Proposition 5.3.5.12, printed p. 408. Read online; not archived in literature/. The assembly and size bookkeeping are agent-written.

proof.text: Local smallness from step 1, existence of filtered colimits from step 2, and the essentially small compact generating subcategory of steps 4-6 give $\kappa$-accessibility by [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Together with all small simplicial colimits from step 2 this is presentability. The $\mathcal U$-small family $\mathcal G$ itself suffices for the generation assertion, since step 6 chose its apices in that family. If $D=\varnothing$, density uses the empty diagram and the family contains its colimit; the same filtered presentation applies. All choices, diagrams and cardinal bounds were made relative to $\mathcal U$, with $\mathcal V$ used only as an ambient universe. The pair $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$ was arbitrary subject to $D$ being $\mathcal U$-small. For any larger universe $\mathcal W$ containing $\mathcal U$, choose an ambient universe $\mathcal W^+$ containing $\mathcal W$. Then $D$ is $\mathcal W$-small, so the universally quantified conclusion just established specializes to the pair $(\mathcal W,\mathcal W^+)$: $\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal W})$ has all $\mathcal W$-small colimits and a $\mathcal W$-small family generating it under $\mathcal W$-small $\kappa_{\mathcal W}$-filtered colimits, for an uncountable regular $\kappa_{\mathcal W}\in\mathcal W$. Its generators and cardinal are allowed to depend on $\mathcal W$. This is the final universe assertion. At no stage was $D$ required to be the nerve of an ordinary category.
